metadata.title: CLS — General-purpose programming language
metadata.description: A statically typed language with a JIT interpreter that runs at the speed of C and Rust. Easy, modular and cross-platform by nature.

hero.subtitle: CLS is a general-purpose, statically typed programming language with a JIT interpreter that runs at the speed of C and Rust. Clean syntax, cross-platform and extensible with native code.

features.title: Built for everything
features.subtitle: CLS combines the comfort of a modern language with the performance of a JIT interpreter that runs at the speed of C and Rust.

facil.title: Clean syntax
facil.description: Clear, predictable syntax, arrow functions and optional types. From zero to productive in a day.

tipado.title: Statically typed
tipado.description: Compile-time type checking, TypeScript-style. Dynamism only exists if you declare it with `any`.

ligero.title: Lightweight
ligero.description: A small runtime and a minimal binary. Ideal for scripts, plugins, CLI tools and embedded systems.

multiplataforma.title: Cross-platform
multiplataforma.description: The same code runs on Windows, Linux and macOS. Native compilation per platform and architecture.

ffi.title: Interoperability
ffi.description: Bindings for other languages and extensions to load native code directly from CLS.

cmx.title: Native CMX
cmx.description: Layout from code: JSX-like markup in the language itself to build interfaces with `CmxValue`.

pipeline.title: How it works
pipeline.subtitle: From source code to execution through a clear, testable pipeline.

step1.title: Lexer + Parser
step1.description: Your `.clsx` code is tokenized and parsed into a serializable AST.

step2.title: Type checker
step2.description: Static type checking, TypeScript-style with unions, generics and literals.

step4.title: JIT interpreter
step4.description: A JIT interpreter that runs at the speed of C and Rust. Compilation to native binaries is in development.

cta.title: Ready to write CLS?
cta.subtitle: Install the CLI, create your first project and run CLS at the speed of C and Rust.

footer.tagline: A general-purpose, modular and cross-platform programming language.

about.title: About CLS
about.subtitle: A general-purpose, statically typed language with a JIT interpreter that runs at the speed of C and Rust.
about.philosophy1: General purpose: scripting, plugins, CLI tools, apps and more, all with the same language.
about.philosophy2: Statically typed by default: compile-time checking, with `any` as the only dynamic escape.
about.philosophy3: Cross-platform by nature: the same code runs on Windows, Linux and macOS, without heavyweight virtual machines.
about.philosophy4: Extensible: bindings for other languages, native code loading and host nodes built by the community.
about.layersSubtitle: A clean separation between the language, the runtime and the host — designed so you can build your own nodes.

layer1.title: cls-core
layer1.description: The language: lexer, parser, type checker, optimizer and the JIT interpreter. Environment-agnostic.

layer2.title: cls-runtime
layer2.description: The runtime: JIT interpreter, values, stdlib, GC and sandboxed VFS.

layer3.title: nodes
layer3.description: The hosts: clx (dev CLI) and clxr (lightweight runtime). Build your own to embed CLS anywhere: FS, network, CLI, config and more.

about.roadmapSubtitle: What is already done and what's next.
about.f1: JIT interpreter at the speed of C and Rust — done.
about.f2: Static type checker + name resolver + optimizer — done.
about.f3: Native AOT backend: a binary per platform and architecture — in development.
about.f4: Stdlib: system modules and intrinsics, yet to be defined.
about.f5: Modules, imports, exports and user modules.
about.extra: LSP + VS Code extension + type maps + async/await + CMX + errors with traces
